summary: Parallel promote handshake delay evicts explicit model pin for tenant during canary weight sweep
description: Issue summary: During a scheduled canary weight sweep + bulk promote that ran concurrently, one NovaChat tenant observed that their per-request explicit model_version pin was ignored and requests were routed to a legacy/degraded variant. Impact: customer-facing sessions saw mixed outputs and 15-20% of streaming sessions were served by a deprecated variant for ~18 minutes, causing a quality regression and billing inconsistency. Observed at ~2026-03-12T14:05-14:23 UTC in us-east (prod).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer submits requests with explicit request header X-Model-Version: redwood/gptx-7b@v1.4.2.
2) Orchestrator receives a parallel bulk promote job and a canary weight sweep (internal schedule).
3) Control-plane snapshot merge and edge cookie rewriting occur in overlapping windows.
4) Some requests evaluate routing before the final promote snapshot commit and pick a fallback (legacy variant).
Expected: explicit per-request model_version pin must always take precedence and not be evicted by concurrent promote mechanics.

comments: Support (Ana Martinez) - 2026-03-12T14:18Z: Received alert from NovaChat CS. They report mixed-model outputs and that they include explicit request pins. Investigating routing history and control-plane commits.

SRE (Ravi Shah) - 2026-03-12T14:27Z: Observed overlapping promote and canary jobs. Early hypothesis: snapshot merge order + edge cookie domain rewrite created a transient key mismatch so pin lookup returned empty and fallback logic applied. Collecting routing traces and KV cache metrics.

Customer (NovaChat - Jordan Li) - 2026-03-12T14:38Z: We saw degraded quality on ~18% of sessions and noticed artifacts in multi-turn chat when the older variant responded. We are paused on canary until resolved.

SRE (Ravi Shah) - 2026-03-12T15:05Z: Applied emergency force-reconcile for affected tenants. Short-term mitigation: reconcile job re-applies tenant pinned_version to routing cache. Will monitor for recurrence.
investigation_notes: Timeline: promote job launched at ~14:05 UTC; control-plane commit seal delayed by ~1.3s due to snapshot merge backpressure; during that window edge-proxy header normalization and cookie domain rotation were performed by a separate job. The pin resolution RPC consults a control-plane cache keyed by (tenant, cookie_namespace, session_token). The cookie rotation produced a transient namespace mismatch meaning pinned key was not found. Fallback routes then applied degraded variant. Root causes identified: 1) concurrent promote + cookie-rotation not serialized, 2) reconciler's pin-lookup did not tolerate short-lived key namespace change (no cross-namespace TTL mapping), 3) lack of telemetry correlating cookie-rotation events with pin misses.
resolution: Mitigation applied: force-reconcile job executed to rebind tenant pins to the active routing index (completed 14:20 UTC). Short-term fix: paused scheduled cookie-domain rotations during rolling promotes in us-east and added a guard to serialize promote and cookie-rotation windows. Permanent fix: merged PR to orchestrator to enforce promote->cookie rotation ordering and to make pin-lookup tolerant to recent namespace rotations (github.com/redwood/orchestrator/pull/2134). Added alerting to surface pin-lookup miss rate correlated with cookie-rotation events. Follow-ups: add unit/integration test for concurrent promote+cookie-rotation (owner: Ravi), add customer-facing post-incident note and billing review (owner: CS).
